calibrationDescription: Calibration (Deville and Särndal, 1992) is a reweighting method in which the new weights must ensure that the population totals estimated with them for the auxiliary variables match the true totals of those variables. At the same time, these weights must be as similar as possible to the original design weights of the survey being calibrated, which is achieved by minimizing a distance function between the original and the new weights. Deville and Särndal (1992) present several alternatives for the distance function. The one used here is the Raking distance (Deville, Särndal and Sautory, 1993), which ensures that the estimated totals for the cross-classifications of variables also match the expected totals for those cross-classifications in the population. In practice, it is the reweighting method most widely used by official statistical agencies.

psaTitle: Propensity Score Adjustment with logistic regression
psaDescription: Propensity Score Adjustment (Lee, 2006; Lee and Valliant, 2009) is a method that estimates the (originally unknown) participation probabilities of the individuals in the nonprobability survey. To do so, the nonprobability survey is combined with a probability survey and a predictive model is fitted to predict the probability that an individual in the combined sample belongs to the nonprobability sample. This predictive model can be a logistic regression or any other predictive algorithm; when this option is selected, logistic regression is used to predict the probabilities. This regression requires that there be no missing data, so imputation is performed on each of the independent variables. Numeric variables are imputed with the median and a new variable is created indicating whether the value was missing or not (which is included in the subsequent regression). For non-numeric variables, a new category corresponding to missing data is created. For the latter, all classes whose relative frequency does not exceed 5% are also grouped into a single class called “Infrequent”. When fitting the models, and following the Adjusted Logistic Propensity (ALP) method described in Wang, Valliant and Li (2021), the design weights of the probability survey are taken into account so that the probabilities are correctly scaled to the whole population, rather than only to the number of individuals in both samples combined (which would lead to probabilities larger than they should be). Finally, the probabilities are transformed into weights to be applied to the nonprobability survey. Several transformations have been studied in the literature; this tool uses the formula: Weights = (1 – Probability)/Probability, developed in Schonlau and Couper (2017), which is also the transformation that corresponds to the ALP method.

psaBoostTitle: Propensity Score Adjustment with Gradient Boosting
psaBoostDescription: Propensity Score Adjustment (Lee, 2006; Lee and Valliant, 2009) is a method that estimates the (originally unknown) participation probabilities of the individuals in the nonprobability survey. To do so, the nonprobability survey is combined with a probability survey and a predictive model is fitted to predict the probability that an individual in the combined sample belongs to the nonprobability sample. This predictive model can be a logistic regression or any other predictive algorithm; when this option is selected, the Histogram-Based Gradient Boosting Classification Tree machine learning algorithm (Guryanov, 2019) is used to predict the probabilities. When fitting the models, and following the weighting instructions for the Gradient Boosting algorithm described in Ferri-García et al. (2024), the design weights of the probability survey are taken into account so that the probabilities are correctly scaled to the whole population, rather than only to the number of individuals in both samples combined (which would lead to probabilities larger than they should be). Finally, the probabilities are transformed into weights to be applied to the nonprobability survey. Several transformations have been studied in the literature; this tool uses the formula: Weights = (1 – Probability)/Probability, which corresponds to the Adjusted Logistic Propensity (ALP) method described in Wang, Valliant and Li (2021). This accounts for the fact that the individuals in the nonprobability survey are not part of the target population of the probability survey.

kwDescription: The Kernel Weighting method (Wang et al., 2020; Kern et al., 2021) uses the probabilities of participating in the nonprobability sample provided by the PSA method. Specifically, it computes the differences in that probability between each unit in the probability sample and each unit in the nonprobability sample. These differences are smoothed using a Kernel function, and the final weight for an individual in the nonprobability sample is obtained by summing the design weights of each unit in the probability sample multiplied by the smoothed difference between that unit and the nonprobability sample unit whose weight is being computed. In this option, the participation probabilities obtained with PSA are estimated using a logistic regression model; you can find more information about this method by selecting the "PSA with logistic regression" option.

popSizeDescription: Total number of individuals in the population from which the sample was obtained. If auxiliary data are available, the inferred value based on the selected weight variable is suggested by default. This is the same population total from which the variable totals are inferred, so it should be used when working with inferred totals. For other methods, this value can be left blank, and relative weights will be calculated.

estimationMethodDescription: Texto de ayuda para "Método de estimación". Para poder optimizar las estimaciones hay que haber seleccionado variables armonizadas. Cuando se activa, si los pesos son uniformes se aplica Matching (se predice la variable objetivo en la muestra de referencia con un modelo ajustado según la información de la muestra no probabilística y se estima a partir de ella, como si fuesen los valores reales) y en caso contrario se aplica Training (idéntico al Matching pero el modelo en esta ocasión es ponderado según los pesos que se indiquen). Si los pesos son uniformes, también están disponibles métodos avanzados que estiman intervalos de confianza más precisos a cambio de ser mucho más lentos.
